activity.notes: Puni (Teihotu Matarua) was the great chief of Bora Bora whose forces conquered Raiatea after a multi-year campaign and whose dominance is independently attested when Cook reached the Leeward Islands in 1769. ATLAS uses c.1763-c.1769 as a defensible evidence window, not as a fabricated complete reign. The polity is Bora Bora rather than back-projecting the later nineteenth-century formal Kingdom of Bora Bora.

sources.title: The Polynesian 'Prince' Who Took 18th-Century England by Storm
sources.citation_text: Smithsonian Magazine describes the conquest of Raiatea around 1763 by Bora Bora invaders under the great chief Puni.

sources.title: ANA'ITE Polynesian scientific digital library — Teihotu Matarua dit Puni
sources.citation_text: University of French Polynesia material identifies Teihotu Matarua, called Puni, as a major Bora Bora warrior whose eighteenth-century campaigns subjugated Raiatea and most Leeward Islands.
